scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they suddenly cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2) or anything else in the partner AS. pc1 can still
ping its own gateway 195.11.14.1 normally. The partner operator
reports their side is healthy internally: pc2 still reaches its
gateway 200.1.1.1 fine. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router1

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 bgpd
Mechanism: router1 (AS 1) is pc1's only gateway and the local eBGP
  speaker toward router2 (AS 2) over the 193.10.11.0/24 inter-AS
  link. With bgpd dead on router1, the eBGP session to router2
  drops: router1 loses the learned route to 200.1.1.0/24 and stops
  advertising 195.11.14.0/24, so router2 withdraws it too. Traffic
  between pc1 and pc2 fails in both directions. Local segments are
  unaffected (pc1<->195.11.14.1 and pc2<->200.1.1.1 still work).
Localization: router1
Root cause: bgpd not running on router1
Fix: restart FRR on router1 (`service frr restart`)

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router1 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router2 re-establishes, router1 re-learns and re-advertises
the inter-AS prefixes, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. router2 needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: bgpd / BGP daemon not running
bonus-rules-out-link: notes the inter-AS link (router1 eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon failure from a link cut

agent.diagnosis_text:
The bgpd process on router1 was killed approximately 90 seconds after lab startup
(at 13:24:51 per the FRR log), and watchfrr — the daemon supervisor responsible for
restarting crashed FRR daemons — was also killed, so bgpd was never respawned. This
is confirmed by multiple lines of evidence: `ps aux` on router1 shows zebra and mgmtd
running but no bgpd process; `show running-config` returns no BGP stanza (because bgpd
itself is the daemon that would answer); the zebra log records
"Client 'bgp' encountered an error and is shutting down" at exactly 13:24:51; and no
watchfrr process appears in the process table despite its PID file existing in
/var/run/frr/. The on-disk /etc/frr/frr.conf is intact and correct (router bgp 1,
neighbor 193.10.11.2 remote-as 2, network 195.11.14.0/24), so the configuration
itself is not the problem.

With bgpd dead, router1 has no BGP routes — its RIB contains only the two directly
connected prefixes (193.10.11.0/24 and 195.11.14.0/24). Router2's BGP neighbor entry
for 193.10.11.1 is stuck in the Active state as it repeatedly tries but fails to open
a TCP session to port 179 on router1. Neither side installs inter-AS routes, so
packets from pc1 destined for 200.1.1.0/24 hit router1 with no matching route and
generate "Destination Net Unreachable" ICMP messages back to pc1.

Root cause: bgpd and watchfrr were killed on router1, permanently dropping the eBGP
session to router2 and blocking automatic recovery.

Corrective fix: Restart watchfrr and bgpd on router1 — either via
`service frr restart` or by manually launching bgpd
(`/usr/lib/frr/bgpd -d -F traditional --daemon -A 127.0.0.1`) followed by
watchfrr. The existing frr.conf will be loaded automatically and the BGP session
with router2 will re-establish, restoring the 200.1.1.0/24 route on router1 and
the 195.11.14.0/24 route on router2.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies router1 as the affected device, describing bgpd and watchfrr being killed on router1.
